### Description

Notes, paper summaries, ideas and to-do lists tend to pile up across scattered files, hard to search and harder to connect. Obsidian is a free note-taking app that keeps them in one linked, searchable place, stored as plain text files on your own computer.

In this hands-on workshop for researchers (no prior experience needed), you learn to set up and structure your own notebook and link related notes, ideas and papers so they're easy to find again. You also build a daily-note workflow to plan your days and track tasks, and use templates for notes you write often. You leave with a starter setup and materials to build on.

## Basic markdown syntax

You can use the following basic formatting syntax to format the text in your
Obsidian notes

````md
# Heading 1
## Heading 2
### Heading 3

**bold** and *italic*   -> Hotkeys: Ctrl/Cmd + B and Ctrl/Cmd + I

- list item
- list item

1. numbered list item
2. numbered list item

- [ ] A task

[A link to a website](https://google.com) -> Hotkey: Ctrl/Cmd + K

[[Another note]] -> A link to another note in your vault

```r
# An R code snippet
mean(1:3)
```

````

### Get started

- Install Obsidian from [https://obsidian.md/](https://obsidian.md/)
- Get the Obsidian demo vault for academic notetaking from [Github](https://github.com/selinaZitrone/notebook_demo)
  - Read the README file for a step-by-step guide on how to download and open the vault in Obsidian
  - Have a look at the "Get Started" files in the demo vault for explanations and step-by-step guides
- A good [tutorial video for Obsidian beginners](https://www.youtube.com/embed/OUrOfIqvGS4)
- [Step-by-Step guide](https://elizabethbutlermd.com/obsidian-notes/) on how to get started with Obsidian in written form
